properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 8:59PM PDT until October 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

- At 9:30 PM MDT Monday the stage was 9.3 feet.

at 9:30 PM MDT Monday was 9.7 feet.

afternoon.

feet on 05/18/1944.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 945 AM MDT.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 8:40PM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be through
Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal Flood
Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf develops.
The Coastal Flood Advisory may also need to be extended beyond
Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Caribbean Waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the Coastal Waters of Saint Croix; Coastal Waters of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 26 at 11:25PM AST until October 27 at 12:30AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
SMWSJU

The National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...
Coastal Waters of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* Until 1230 AM AST.

* At 1125 PM AST, A severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over the offshore Caribbean waters of
Puerto Rico from around 10 nmi from the coastline from Cabo Rojo to
Penuelas to around 17N, moving northwest at 15-20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to
17N, including the coastal waters of Saint Croix and Coastal Waters
of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with this storm.

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge affecting
Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge.

* WHEN...From this evening to Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, after which the
flood plain between the levees begins to flood.  No damage is
expected. At 15.5 feet, the river reaches minor flood stage, and
flooding between the levees occurs.  No damage to structures is
expected. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage,
inundating the plain between the levees.  Erosion of the levees is
likely.  Water may seep through the levees, flooding adjacent
farmland. At 22.9 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.  While
water remains between the levees at Presidio, areas downstream may
experience significant flooding.  FM 170 downstream of Presidio
will flood in low spots.  Farmland along the river will be
inundated. At 25.0 feet, the river remains between the levees at
Presidio, although continued flows at this level could cause damage
to the levees.  FM 170 downstream will likely be flooded and
impassable in spots.  Farmland around the river will continue to
inundate. At 25.8 feet, the river reaches record stage for the
period of record (1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but
the exact stage is unknown.  FM 170 will be flooded downstream of
Presidio.  Farmland around the river will remain inundated. At 28.2
feet, the river reaches record stage for the period of record
(1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but the exact stage is
unknown.  FM 170 remains flooded downstream of Presidio.  Farmland
adjacent to the river remains inundated. At 30.0 feet, The top of
the levee is reached, and water will begin to overtop the levees.
Major flooding of Presidio and surrounding farmland is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM CDT Monday was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 4.1 feet (1.2
meters) Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet (4.7 meters).
- Flood History...No available flood history.

properties.areaDesc: Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 26 at 9:38PM AST until October 28 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
